title: Deepak Chetty @ vs Marthama Bisoi @ Putuki on 8 October, 2026

paragraphs.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF ORISSA AT CUTTACK
 TRP(C) No.315 of 2026
 CNR No. ODHC010714072026
 Deepak Chetty @ ..... Petitioner
 Deepak Kumar Chetty
 Mr. Bikash Karna, Advocate
 -versus-
 Marthama Bisoi @ Putuki ..... Opposite Party
 Bisoi


 CORAM:
 JUSTICE SANJAY KUMAR MISHRA

 ORDER
01. This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.
2. Heard learned Counsel for the Petitioner.

3. This transfer petition has been preferred by the
 Petitioner-husband under Section 24 of the Code of Civil
 Procedure, 1908, seeking transfer of proceeding of C.S.
 (MAT) No.02 of 2026, preferred by the Opposite Party-
 wife under Section 10 of the Indian Divorce Act, 1869 for
 dissolution of marriage, pending in the Court of learned
 District Judge, Malkangiri, to the Court of learned
 District Judge, Koraput on the grounds detailed in the
 transfer petition.

4. Reiterating the grounds urged in the transfer
 petition, learned Counsel for the Petitioner submits, the
 Petitioner is a daily labourer having uncertain income.
 That apart, the application for divorce, i.e., C.S. (MAT)
 No.02 of 2026 has been instituted by Opposite Party-wife


 Page 1 of 3.
 at Malkangiri. He has no relation or family members at
Malkangiri, where he can stay on the date of attending
the Court proceeding. That part, the distance from his
village, i.e., Lulla, in the district of Koraput, to the Court
of learned District Judge, Malkangiri would be around
150 KMs.

5. Neither it has been pleaded in the transfer petition
nor the learned Counsel for the Petitioner is able to
apprise the Court as to the status of the Opposite Party-
wife, her income and other aspects, which may be good
ground to consider the prayer for transfer, in addition to
the grounds urged in the transfer petition, to
demonstrate before this Court that the Opposite Party-
wife is in a better footing than the Petitioner, deserving
consideration of the prayer for transfer of proceeding
from Malkangiri to Koraput. Rather, in paragraph-7 of
the transfer petition, it has been fairly pleaded that as
per the settled position of law, while considering the
application for transfer of matrimonial proceedings,
wife's convenience is to be looked at.

6. In the circumstances, after going through the
grounds urged in the transfer petition, after hearing
learned Counsel for the Petitioner and taking note of the
settled position of law, this Court is not inclined to
entertain the prayer made in the transfer petition.
7. Accordingly, the transfer petition stands dismissed.

8. However, it is made clear that dismissal of the
transfer petition shall not be a bar for the Petitioner to
move appropriate application before the learned District

 Page 2 of 3.
 Judge, Malkangiri in C.S. (MAT) No.02 of 2026 to permit
 the Petitioner-husband to appear through virtual mode
 at appropriate stage, in case he faces any difficulty on
 any date to appear physically before the said Court.

9. Accordingly, the learned District Judge, Malkangiri is
 requested to explore the facility of video conferencing
 available in the said Court and allow the Petitioner to
 appear through video conferencing mode, following the
 guidelines prescribed under the "High Court of Orissa and
 District Courts Use of Electronic Communication and
 Audio-Video Electronic Means Rules, 2025", if it is so
 required and prayed by the Petitioner.

10. However, on the dates of effective hearing, i.e., for
 examination and cross-examination of witnesses and other
 purposes, for which his presence may be required by the
 Court and if it is so ordered, the Petitioner so also his
 witnesses, if any, shall remain physically present before the
 learned District Judge, Malkangiri.

11. I.A. No.332 of 2026 also stands disposed of
 accordingly.

Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on
 proper application.

Kanhu (S.K. Mishra)
 Judge
